reviewer_role: release gatekeeper with AI Council perspectives
decision_scope: Campaign 11 exact-row-9 residual-plus-LayerNorm candidate, retained failures, integrated evidence, documentation, and terminal closure gates
facts: Fifty-one protected contract tests passed before candidate work, and the active and detached starting workspaces matched the selected Campaign 10 fingerprint.
The fresh row-9 profile measured 5769.588 us of residual-add plus native-LayerNorm time, 19.095 percent of 30214.766 us model device time across 30 forwards.
EXP-025-I1 changes only one exact runtime/model predicate for batch 64, sequence 128, width 128, one head, FFN 128, four layers, causal eager CUDA float32 inference.

The isolated candidate and active transplant each passed direct route, strict boundary, all 18 seed-scale-padding stress scenarios, the 40-test affected suite, and complete final-matrix correctness gates with zero failed elements.

Two unchanged 300-sample controls measured 0.815776 and 0.816160 ms optimized median, a 0.047 percent spread. The active 0.717648 ms result is 12.049 percent below their mean and within 0.007 percent of the isolated 0.717696 ms candidate.
Both controls, the isolated candidate, and active integration use the same 29360128-byte optimized incremental peak allocation; the active target run records 1240 Triton attention calls.
Two active profiles each record 240 fused residual-normalization launches, 30 native norms, and 120 Triton calls. Mean subsystem time falls from 5765.324 to 3357.389 us, or 41.766 percent.

The active profile pair's top-level model event is 2.544 percent above the two baseline profiles because one active snapshot is slow. This variance is disclosed and the release claim rests on the counterbalanced CUDA-event timing rather than the top-level profiler event.

Primary and confirmation final matrices each pass all 13 executable rows plus the one authorized resource skip with zero of 938885120 failed elements at 1.977420x and 1.986499x and identical aggregate backend counts.

Organizer default passes 5 of 5 at 1.385x, source-derived passes all 28 executable cases at 1.206505x, and four held-out matrices pass all seven cases while long-causal remains in a 1.198x to 1.204x band.
Inherited row-5, row-6, row-8, and row-11 profiles retain exact fusion, projection, and backend counts; long gates pass at 1.880x, 1.546x, and 4.710x for rows 5, 6, and 11.
Artifact and notebook contracts pass 19 of 19 and the complete repository suite passes 148 of 148 tests with 14 upstream deprecation warnings.
Launcher, raw-byte newline, JSON-nesting, quoting, and stale-artifact failures remain in the immutable ledger with corrected passing attempts; no failed evidence was deleted or relabeled.
EXP-026 row-10 fusion was deliberately unrun because its declared fallback condition became false when EXP-025 produced an accepted winner.

council_review.requirements: The selected candidate preserves the organizer harness, comparator, resource-skip rule, backend accounting, public model contract, and exact inference-only support envelope while satisfying the reproducible target-performance threshold.
council_review.architecture: Reusing the accepted fused residual-normalization primitive behind one exact row-9 predicate is a bounded dispatch extension. It does not broaden attention arithmetic, packed-QKV policy, public APIs, state dictionaries, dependencies, or persistence surfaces.
council_review.implementation: The source change is one exact predicate plus one union term, with three focused tests covering selected routing, unsupported boundaries, and numerical stress. Normal PyTorch behavior remains the fallback everywhere else.
council_review.security_privacy: No dependency, credential, network, authentication, authorization, permission, telemetry, external-system, or sensitive-data surface changed.
council_review.testing_qa: Provenance, direct, boundary, stress, affected-suite, counterbalanced timing, memory, repeated profile, two final matrices, four held-out matrices, long-causal, organizer-default, source-derived, inherited-route, notebook, artifact-contract, and complete-suite gates support selection.
council_review.user_docs: Requirements, README, design, report, compliance, Devpost, demo, result index, notebook, comparison, validation, loop plan, history, and comprehensive run-through identify Campaign 11, disclose historical and current failures, and bind selected claims to the current fingerprint.
council_review.devils_advocate: The exact guard adds benchmark-specific maintenance, one active top-level profile is slow, and held-out aggregate geomeans vary from 1.340x to 1.515x. These concerns prevent universal claims but do not invalidate the 12.049 percent tightly counterbalanced row-9 latency reduction, stable 41.766 percent subsystem mechanism, unchanged peak allocation, exact backend counts, and zero-error complete matrices.

conditions: Validate this review, Campaign 11 artifact contracts, and the complete repository suite through immutable attempts.
Complete workflow validation, append and validate graph closure, reconcile campaign accounting, and run scoped diff hygiene before declaring Campaign 11 closed.
Keep row-9 fusion exact; any neighboring or broader fusion requires fresh profile, correctness, boundary, timing, memory, and complete-matrix evidence.
Do not revive EXP-026 inside Campaign 11 because its conditional fallback is false; a later campaign requires a new profile and scope decision.
Do not perform any commit, push, tag, release, branch creation, history rewrite, deployment, or public action without a separate explicit request.
residual_risks: Performance is specific to the recorded RTX 5070 Ti software and driver environment.
The organizer still omits dtype, padding, timing, tolerance, backward, and evaluator-hardware policy from the final table.
The implementation is forward inference only and exact-shape fusion adds benchmark-specific maintenance cost.
Top-level profiler and whole-matrix geomeans are affected by timing-window noise and must not be presented as causal candidate comparisons.
The public repository, organizer-policy clarification, video, and Devpost publication remain external holds.
